what: Effect of an Adaptive Game-Based Math Learning App on Students’ Learning
title: Item level treatment effect heterogeneity
text: recent block randomized control trial, Bang, Li, Flynn (2022) investigated whether using Math Academy, personalized adaptive learning app, improve math achievement learning engagement K-1 students (n=505 treatment, n=481 control). Math Academy supplemented school curricula game-based activities, performance dashboards teachers, offline additional learning activities. Blocking school grade, teachers cluster randomized treatment (21 classrooms) control (20 classrooms). Treatment teachers tasked using Math Academy least 60 minutes per week. Control teachers implemented whatever math curricula district used. intervention took place February June 2019. total, 41 classrooms 11 elementary schools participated. Math achievement measured pre-test post-test using 38 multiple-choice items selected Certica assessment item bank. Items selected aligned Common Core State Standards K-2 targeted specific Math Academy learning objectives. Students 30-45 minutes complete assessment. Responses coded 0 (incorrect) 1 (correct) analyses. Bang colleagues (2022) estimated simple treatment effect computing difference mean un-weighted post-test total scores: TreatmentEffect=TotalScore¯treat−TotalScore¯control TreatmentEffect = \overline{\text{TotalScore}}_{\text{treat}} - \overline{\text{TotalScore}}_{\text{control}}=20.97−20.08=0.89= 20.97 - 20.08 = 0.89  Dividing pooled standard deviation gives measure effect size (d): d=TEsdp=0.898.09=0.11 d = \frac{TE}{sd_p} = \frac{0.89}{8.09} = 0.11 findings indicate students using Math Academy greater math achievement scores students , difference relatively small. following analysis examine whether effect size robust item-level sources variability may generalize measures Math achievement (.e., tests different questions).

title: robustDIF Technical Notes
text: robust DIF estimator θ̃\tilde\theta can computed using IRLS based weighted mean definition given . IRLS algorithm follows: Initialize θ(0)\theta^{(0)} set iteration counter t=0t = 0. Compute standardized residuals ui(t)=(Yi−θ(t))/siu_i^{(t)} = (Y_i - \theta^{(t)}) / s_i. Compute weights wi(θ(t))=ψ(ui(t))/ui(t)w_i(\theta^{(t)}) = \psi(u_i^{(t)}) / u_i^{(t)} wi*(0)≡1w^*_i(0) \equiv 1. Update θ(t+1)=∑=1mwi(θ(t))Yi\theta^{(t+1)} = \sum_{= 1}^{m} w_i(\theta^{(t)})\, Y_i wi(θ(t))=wi*(θ(t))/si2∑j=1mwj*(θ(t))/sj2w_i(\theta^{(t)}) = \frac{w^*_i(\theta^{(t)}) / s_i^2}{\sum_{j=1}^{m} w^*_j(\theta^{(t)}) / s_j^2}. |θ(t+1)−θ(t)|<ϵ|\theta^{(t+1)} - \theta^{(t)}| < \epsilon stop; else set t=t+1t = t + 1 return step 2. algorithm converged, set θ̃=θ(t+1)\tilde\theta = \theta^{(t+1)}. Item-level DIF tests can conducted using Wald test statistic given multi-parameter variant given Halpin (2022).

title: Differential Item Functioning Using Robust Scaling
text: R package provides functions assessing differential item functioning (DIF) item response theory (IRT) models using methods robust statistics. Based paper: Halpin, P.F. (2022) Differential Item Functioning Via Robust Scaling. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.04598. Published Psychometrika 2024 title. Recent additions: Support graded response model Read functions mirt lavaan Test whether naive estimates impact affected DIF (delta_test) development: S3 rdif class supporting methods Multi-parameter tests DIF / measurement invariance Additional models multiple groups Technical notes: HTML: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/peterhalpin/robustDIF/blob/master/technical-notes.html

Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-0317-7, Chap. 6). Robustness achieved downweighting items exhibit DIF, amounts flagging items DIF estimation scaling parameter. Following estimation scaling parameter, Wald tests DIF can implemented. type DIF tested depends choice scaling parameter. Let $\theta_g \thicksim N(\mu_g, \sigma_g)$ aiga_{ig} digd_{ig} denote item slope intercept/thresholds respectively. choices scaling parameters corresponding item-level scaling functions follows. illustration uses d_fun3. function sensitive intercept-DIF slope-DIF.

title: Differential Item Functioning Using Robust Scaling
text: scaling parameter can estimated using rdif. Estimation uses iteratively reweighted least squares Tukey’s bisquare. tuning parameter bisquare set via desired false positive rate flagging items DIF (alpha). See technical notes details. estimated scaling parameter approximately 0.38 (SE = 0.09). data generating value 0.50. Wald tests indicate first item flagged DIF 5% level. item downweighted zero estimation scaling parameter (based alpha = .05). Note output, delta estimated scaling parameter subtracted value item-level scaling function.

text: three-element list: par.names: list internal original parameter names. est: list (one element per group) data frames containing item parameters row (a1, d1, d2, ...). var.cov: list (one element per group) covariance matrices corresponding parameter vectors.

title: Extract and format item parameter estimates and their covariance matrix — get_model_parms
text: function takes fitted 1-factor multigroup model list fitted 1-factor single group models. factor must standardized (.e., variance = 1) covariance matrix asymptotically correct. Currently, function accepts: mirt object class SingleGroupClass MultipleGroupClass SE = TRUE (return covariance matrix) itemtype combination "2PL", "graded", "gpcm". lavaan object estimated cfa std.lv = TRUE. cluster supplied mirt fits, covariance matrix computed using cluster-robust sandwich estimator Oakes bread cluster-summed empirical scores. CR1 finite-sample correction applied: (G/(G-1)) * ((N-1)/(N-p)), G number clusters, N number observations, p number free parameters. possible use fits software robustDIF functions, parameter estimates covariance matrices must formatted identically returned get_model_parms. details, see documentation example dataset rdif.eg.
